notes:
I couldn't write these notes this time. My first attempt to open the source pages was blocked straight away with a message saying I had no tool calls left for this turn. That means I haven't read any pages, including Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary, Matthew Henry, Wesley or Precept Austin.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to cite a URL for every point. Writing commentary from memory would break both rules, so I've left it out rather than give you uncited notes.

**Pages I planned to read first:**
- enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ecclesiastes-4/
- biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/ecclesiastes/4.htm (also the /ellicott/, /pulpit/ and /mhc/ versions)
- preceptaustin.org/ecclesiastes-4-commentary
- studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/ecclesiastes-4.html (Wesley's Notes, for the Methodist view)

**Searches I planned after those:**
- **Verse 12 ("a cord of three strands"):** what the different traditions say about reading it as marriage, as Christ in a marriage, or as the Trinity (gotquestions.org, desiringgod.org, thegospelcoalition.org, the Catholic and Orthodox sites)
- **Verses 2–3 (the dead and the unborn being better off):** how pastors handle these (ligonier.org, gty.org, spurgeon.org)
- **Verses 4–8 (envy, work and wealth):** what the sites say about prosperity teaching
- **Verses 13–16 (the poor youth and the old king):** whether any page names a historical king, and the NET Bible's notes on the Hebrew
- **Church Fathers:** for example, Jerome's commentary on Ecclesiastes (newadvent.org, ccel.org)

If you ask again in a new message, I'll start with these sources and write the notes verse by verse, with a URL after every point.
